findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — Return value shape silently diverges by env config: the CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT branch returns a raw, un-JSON-parsed `fetch` Response while the default branch returns the provider SDK's response object (e.g. GaxiosResponse with a synchronous `.data`), so callers written against the old shape (e.g. googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 `const token = res?.data`) silently get `undefined` and break token refresh for every self-hoster who enables credential sync

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — When the refreshed token response has no `refresh_token`, the code hardcodes the literal string `"refresh_token"` as the stored refresh token instead of preserving the existing credential's refresh token, silently persisting a bogus placeholder that will break all subsequent OAuth refresh attempts for that credential

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — [z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` compute static/literal object keys from stringifying Zod schema instances rather than defining a catchall/record schema, so `minimumTokenResponseSchema` does not actually require an expiry field or allow arbitrary extra properties as the comments claim — the documented minimum contract for CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT responses is not enforced

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` is unguarded (no try/catch), so an invalid payload throws a raw ZodError producing Next.js's default unhandled-exception response instead of the endpoint's own consistent `{ message }` JSON error envelope used for every other failure case

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` is unguarded; a malformed or undecryptable `keys` value throws an uncaught error, yielding an undocumented 500 instead of the endpoint's standard `{ message }` error shape

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added Next.js API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the `handler` does not check `req.method` at all. It always proceeds to `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`, which will throw if the request is a non-POST (e.g., GET with no/invalid body), resulting in a 500 rather than a clean 405. This is a real behavioral defect for an externally exposed webhook endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` is unguarded; a malformed or undecryptable `keys` value throws an uncaught error, yielding an undocumented 500 instead of the endpoint's standard `{ message }` error shape

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler decrypts and parses `reqBody.keys` via `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` with no try/catch or error handling around either operation. If `symmetricDecrypt` throws (e.g., wrong/empty `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, invalid ciphertext) or if the decrypted plaintext is not valid JSON, `JSON.parse` will throw and Next.js will return an unhandled 500 response rather than the explicit `{ message }` JSON used elsewhere in this endpoint (e.g., 403/404 branches). This behavior is directly visible from the diff and represents a real robustness/correctness issue for malformed input.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `redirectUri` changed from `WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback`` to `WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback`` while `appConfig` is still imported/used in the file. This isn’t demonstrably broken from the diff alone (the route folder is `zoho-bigin`, so the literal likely matches today), but it does introduce an unnecessary hardcoded slug that could drift from `appConfig.slug` in forks/renames and then break the OAuth redirect URI without any compile-time signal.
